concept_weaknesses: The $150,000 request exceeds the stated award maximum of $75,000; revise the request and budget to fit the opportunity or clarify whether other funding will support the full project.

The proposed expansion to 10 schools and 500 students is much larger than the documented reach and partnerships: 312 students were tutored in 2025, and MOUs are listed for two schools. Explain how the expansion will be staffed and supported.

Daily tutoring across 10 schools for four months may be difficult to deliver with 30 staff-capacity hours per month and existing volunteers; provide a feasible staffing, volunteer, and implementation plan.

The outcome targets—70% of tutored students gaining a DIBELS benchmark level and 60% of families attending at least three literacy nights—need a rationale grounded in prior results and a clear measurement plan.
The budget summary is too limited for a $150,000 project and does not explain costs beyond tutoring.
unsupported_claims: “Our program is proven to double reading growth” is not supported by the listed evidence, which reports that pre/post DIBELS assessments were conducted for 241 students but provides no results.
“Our tutoring model produced gains for most students in 2025” is not substantiated by the listed evidence because assessment outcomes are not provided.
The claim that fewer than half of K-3 students at partner schools read at grade level is attributed to school-reported data, but that data is not among the listed evidence assets.
concerns: The opportunity requires two letters of support and a logic model; these are not listed among the organization’s evidence assets, so confirm they can be obtained and prepared by the deadline.
The proposal emphasizes tutoring but should also explain how it will deliver and measure the family literacy engagement that is a stated funder priority.
rationale: The organization meets all stated hard eligibility criteria: it is a 501(c)(3), its budget is below $3 million, and it serves Connecticut residents. The concept aligns well with the funder’s K-3 literacy, family engagement, and measurable-outcomes priorities, but requires substantial revision before submission, particularly to fit the award ceiling and substantiate the proposed scale, outcomes, and impact claims.
